title: Update docs + quickstarts for standardized SDK auth/retry/timeout configuration (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Ibrahim Khan
description:
Customer-facing docs + quickstarts currently diverge across languages (different env var names, different retry defaults, different timeout semantics, and inconsistent streaming guidance). Update docs site and quickstarts to reflect the standardized SDK behavior and configuration knobs across Python/TypeScript/Go.

Scope:
- Auth: env var naming + precedence; explicit param vs env; safe logging guidance.
- Retries: default retry policy, configuration fields, Retry-After behavior, and streaming retry guidance.
- Timeouts: timeout model and recommended defaults; how to set overall/connect/read in each language.
- Standard logging fields / hooks: request_id + retry_count + timeout_ms.

Non-goals:
- Redesign docs IA or create net-new product pages. Keep to targeted edits + cross-links to migration notes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Same option names and conceptual behavior are shown across all 3 language examples, even if the underlying HTTP client differs.
- Each doc page includes a short “Defaults” section (retries, timeouts) + “How to override” snippets.
- Quickstarts (hosted API + streaming) include explicit retry/timeout configuration and request_id logging.
- Migration note is linked from all updated pages; quickstarts reference it in an “Upgrading?” callout.
- Docs reviewed by DevEx + SRE (retry storm messaging) + Security (auth/env var + secret handling).

Primary outputs:
- Docs PR(s) in redwood-docs
- Quickstarts PR(s) in redwood-quickstarts
- Examples PR(s) in redwood-examples (optional but recommended for idempotency + safe retry patterns)

Tracking links:
- Confluence: eng-developer-experience/docs-site/sdk-migration-notes-auth-retry-timeout.json
- Confluence standard: architecture-and-standards/api-standards/sdk-retry-timeout-standard.json
- Confluence security: security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sdk-auth-resolution-and-secret-handling.json
implementation_notes:
Edits focus on aligning wording and examples with the approved standards/ADRs:

Docs updates (redwood-docs):
- Retries + timeouts page: add consistent defaults table (max_attempts, base_delay_ms, max_delay_ms, jitter, retryable status codes, respect Retry-After).
- Auth page: document auth resolution order and canonical env var(s); add warning about secret redaction and avoiding logging raw tokens.
- Streaming guide: add section on disconnect handling and conservative retry guidance (idempotency keys; do not automatically retry mid-stream).

Quickstarts updates (redwood-quickstarts):
- Add a “Production settings” snippet in each language quickstart showing:
  - setting API key via env var
  - overriding timeouts
  - customizing retries (or disabling)
  - logging request_id + retry_count (via hook / error fields)
- Ensure streaming quickstart includes cancellation and partial output semantics.

Examples (redwood-examples):
- Add/refresh an example demonstrating safe retry patterns for non-streaming calls + idempotency key guidance.

Content conventions applied:
- Use Redwood terms consistently: “overall timeout” (with connect/read mapping per SDK), “Retry-After”, “request_id”, “idempotency key”
- Avoid implying retries are always safe; include explicit caveats on side effects and streaming.

Review checklist:
- SRE: confirm we are not encouraging aggressive retry behavior; include backoff/jitter language and max attempts.
- Security: confirm env var naming + precedence, error messages do not leak secrets, and docs advise against printing tokens.

- Streaming disconnect/cancellation guidance and conservative retry messaging
- Links to migration notes from updated pages/quickstarts
- Review signoff incorporated from SRE and Security
